title: Narrow the Blast Radius
goal: Raw pointer reads, three containments. Count who has to say 'unsafe' - and how often.
hints: An unsafe fn exports the obligation: every caller must wrap the call. A safe fn with an inner block contains it.
Two dereferences under one contract can share one block - same guarantees, half the ceremony.
explanation: Three containment strategies for the same two dereferences. The unsafe fn pushes the burden outward onto every caller - and the shared test proves it the hard way: it calls read_both without ceremony, so the unsafe-API candidate fails to compile the test at all (E0133 inside the test). The two-block version contains the unsafety but signs the same safety argument twice. The tight single block behind a safe signature is the standard-library pattern: contained, argued once, invisible to callers.
